name: Light Maroon
lede: Light Maroon lightens [[maroon]], and is not to be confused with FireBrick, which Paterson's dictionary separately calls "a light maroon colour."

sections.title: Not the same as FireBrick
sections.body: This name is the modifier *light* set against the base color [[maroon]], recorded in the xkcd 2010 crowd survey [1]. Paterson's dictionary does use the phrase "a light maroon colour" elsewhere, but to describe FireBrick, one of the 140 X11 Color Set names, hex #B22222, a browner red than the #A24857 shown here [2]. The two are unrelated namings that happen to share descriptive words [2]. The ISCC-NBS system's nearest block is "moderate red," 5.1 units away [1]. Nearest on file are [[pomegranate-purple]] and [[pomegranate-purple]], at 2.6 and 2.9 units [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 31 of 23,781 paintings, 0.13 percent, rarer than 63 percent of our named colors; within a single canvas it is a distinct area in 17 of them [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 0.4 percent of that century's 1,674 paintings, 3.3 times the expected rate, and inside a painting it most often plays an accent across its 17 appearances [3]. The earliest dated match is a 1470 panel by Hans Memling, 540 years before the name's 2010 record; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [3]. In printed English the word "maroon" rose fastest in the 1920s, by Google Books counts across all senses of the word, so a color name that is also an everyday word can mislead [3].
